source_text: V. Iratus itaque Probus super fiduciam beatissimi viri, iussit eum etiam gladio percuti. sanctus vero dei martyr, tamquam secundam palmam accipiens, deo gratias agebat dicens: Tibi gratias ago, domine Iesu Christe, qui mihi per varias poenas et tormenta donas tolerantiam et aeternae gloriae me participem efficere dignatus es. et cum venisset ad pontem qui vocatur Basentis, exspolians se vestimenta sua et extendens manus in caelum oravit dicens: Domine Iesu Christe, qui pro mundi salute pati dignatus es, pateant caeli tui, ut suscipiant angeli spiritum servi tui Irenaei, qui propter nomen tuum et plebem tuam productam de ecclesia tua catholica Sirmiensium haec patior. te peto, tuamque deprecor misericordiam, ut et me suscipere et hos in fide tua confirmare digneris. sic itaque percussus gladio a ministris proiectus est in fluvium Savi. VI. Martyrizatus est famulus dei sanctus Irenaeus episcopus civitatis Sirmiensium die VIII. idus Aprilis sub Diocletiano imperatore, agente Probo praeside, regnante domino nostro Iesu Christo; cui est gloria in saecula saeculorum, amen.
pass_a_gloss: Probus, enraged at the resolve of the most blessed man, gave order that he also be struck with the sword. The holy martyr of God, as though taking a second victor's palm, kept giving thanks to God, saying he thanks the Lord Jesus Christ because through manifold punishments and tortures he gives endurance and has counted him worthy to share in eternal glory. When he reached the bridge named Basentis, he stripped off his own clothes and, with hands stretched to heaven, prayed that the Lord Jesus Christ who consented to suffer for the world's salvation would open his heavens so angels would take up the spirit of his servant Irenaeus, who endures this for his name and for his people brought out from his catholic church of the Sirmians, begging his mercy to both take him and make these firm in his faith. So, cut down by the sword by the assistants, he was thrown into the Savi river. The servant of God, holy Irenaeus, bishop of the Sirmian city, was made a martyr on 6 April under Emperor Diocletian when Probus was governor, with our Lord Jesus Christ reigning, to whom belongs glory for ever and ever, amen.
pass_b_english: Then Probus, angered by the most blessed man's firm resolve, ordered him also to be struck down by the sword.

And the holy martyr of God, as if receiving a second palm of victory, gave thanks to God, saying: To you I give thanks, Lord Jesus Christ, who through varied punishments and torments grant me endurance and have deemed me worthy to make me a partaker of eternal glory.

And when he had come to the bridge that is called Basentis, stripping off his garments and stretching his hands toward heaven he prayed, saying: Lord Jesus Christ, who deigned to suffer for the salvation of the world, may your heavens stand open, so that the angels may receive the spirit of your servant Irenaeus, who for your name and for your people led out from your catholic church of the Sirmians endure these things.
You I ask, and your mercy I entreat, that you would deign both to receive me and to confirm these in your faith.
Thus, struck with the sword by the attendants, he was cast into the river Savi.

The servant of God, holy Irenaeus, bishop of the city of the Sirmians, was martyred on the eighth day before the Ides of April under Diocletian the emperor, with Probus acting as governor, while our Lord Jesus Christ reigns, to whom is glory unto ages of ages, amen.

choices.why: super with accusative here expresses motive for anger at his unwavering confession, not merely trust in general

choices.english: as if receiving a second palm of victory
choices.why: tamquam with participle marks comparison to an athlete's prize, fitting a second sentence after earlier torments

choices.term: plebem tuam productam de ecclesia tua catholica Sirmiensium
choices.english: your people led forth from your catholic church of the Sirmians
choices.why: productam agrees with plebem and with de points to a crowd brought out to witness, not a people created by the church
rejected: your people produced by the church
